title: compact delta reporter + rollback suggester for prompt-set regressions
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a compact delta reporter that summarizes prompt-set regressions and a CI hook that suggests rollback patches; opt-in via EVAL_COMPACT_DELTA=true. No API breaking changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Teams running longitudinal prompt-set CI get overwhelmed by large per-example diffs when a model/quantization change causes small but widespread regressions. This PR implements a compact delta reporter that collapses per-example noise into a severity-ranked histogram and a small set of representative exemplars, and a rollback suggester that proposes a minimal patch (prompt removal/restore or model pin) when a severity threshold is exceeded.

What this change does: Implements a new reporter module (reporters/compact_delta_reporter.py) that computes per-prompt composite severity using configurable signals (delta in metric, change frequency across seeds, token-level saliency). The reporter emits a compact JSON summary that the CI hook consumes. Adds a CI adapter (ci/hooks/prompt_regression_gate.py) which evaluates the compact report against policy rules; when policy crosses a soft threshold it annotates the PR with a suggested rollback (linear link + suggested branch name + patch hint). Above hard thresholds the hook blocks merge (soft-fail behavior is opt-in).

Implementation notes: - New config keys under eval.config: compact_delta = {enabled:boolean, severity_weights, exemplar_count, soft_threshold, hard_threshold}. - Small protobuf-compatible summary format to keep artifact sizes small. - Rollback suggester currently supports: pin model version in eval job, revert a prompt change, or attach a recommended prompt whitelist; it emits suggested git diff snippets in the annotation body. - Backwards compatible: existing reporters unchanged; the compact path is an additional artifact consumers can opt into.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for summary aggregation, exemplar selection and severity scoring under tests/test_compact_delta.py. Integration smoke in tests/integration/test_ci_hook.py that simulates a PR with a synthetic regressing prompt set and validates annotation + block behavior. Added a small perf test to ensure reporter run stays under 150ms for 10k prompt samples (benchmarks/compact_delta_perf.md).

Rollout and migration: Feature gated by EVAL_COMPACT_DELTA env var and feature flag in Linear ENG-4310. Will enable on the dev-canaary pipeline for 48 hours, then progressively enable soft-fail mode on staging, finally enabling hard blocking for teams opted into strict CI in two weeks.

Notes for reviewers: The change touches CI and reporter surfaces; please check the config validation logic and the annotation text format (we want deterministic suggested patches). Related: ENG-4273 and SUP-1189 for support escalation automation.

review_comments: Jorge Alvarez: Can we avoid a full token-level diff for every sample? That was costly in earlier runs. Suggest using a heuristic token-saliency sample first.
Maya Chen: Answered: we sample token saliency and then only compute full diffs for top-K exemplars; that logic is in saliency_utils.sample_and_score().
Nina Kapoor: The annotation text looks long; will reviewers read suggested patches? Could we include a short table + link to full artifact?
Maya Chen: Revised annotation to include a 3-line summary + link to compact_summary artifact (GCS). Full diff trimmed to patch hints to keep the PR comment concise.
Samir Rao: CI blocking thresholds need conservative defaults. Request lowering hard_threshold to 0.08 for initial rollout.
Maya Chen: Lowered default hard_threshold in defaults.yaml and documented rollback policy in docs/ci_hooks.md; marked behavior as opt-in.
